I am 74 years old. I never went to school, not even one day. I have been farming this land in Quzhou for 35 years. My farm is 5 mu. I plant 3 mu of spring corn and 2 mu of cotton. There are only two people in my house. My son works in a factory in the city, so I do most of the field work myself. I am old now, but I still know my land well.

I always start from what I did last year. Last year, I put one bag of compound fertilizer on each mu for both crops. For the corn, I added another full bag of urea when the corn was knee-high. For the cotton, I added half a bag of urea when the flowers came out. The harvest was okay — I got about 1,100 jin of corn per mu and about 550 jin of cotton per mu. This year I will do the same thing. Fertilizer costs money, but losing yield is much worse. I would rather put a little too much than too little. A bad harvest is a disaster. Wasting some fertilizer is just money spent.

For seeds, I buy hybrid corn seeds from the dealer in town. Everyone around here plants hybrid corn — the old seeds do not grow well anymore. For cotton, I buy the improved seeds that my neighbor Old Wang used last year. His cotton did very well, so I will copy him.

I have a well, so I can irrigate. Last year I irrigated the corn three times: once right after planting, once when it was growing tall, and once when the ears were filling. For cotton, I also irrigated three times. I will do the same this year. The well water costs diesel, but without water the crops will die in the dry spells.

For pests, the corn does not need much spraying. I spray herbicide once after planting to kill the weeds, and I spray insecticide twice if I see worms in the leaves. Cotton is different. The bollworm is terrible here. Last year I sprayed about eight times during the summer, mixing two medicines in the tank each time. I will do the same this year. If I stop spraying, the worms will eat everything in one week.

Before planting, I hire the tractor man to come rotary-till the fields. It costs about 50 yuan per mu, but the soil needs turning. I cannot do it by hand anymore.

Everything costs money — fertilizer, seeds, diesel for the pump, medicine, machine hire. I have to think about my whole budget. But I know from experience that if I try to save too much on inputs, I will regret it at harvest time.
